RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Central Indiana Ethanol, LLC	

Central Indiana Ethanol, LLC (CIE) is providing this resubmission to satisfy the 5-year requirement. 

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND RESPONSE POLICIES:
CIE has an ongoing commitment to the health and safety of onsite employees and the surrounding community. This commitment is demonstrated in the resources invested in accident prevention, such as personnel training for the proper operation and maintenance of plant equipment and preventative maintenance programs.

CIE has emergency response policies in place that are addressed in the facility's Health and Safety Plan; Industrial Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan; Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan (SPCC); and Emergency Action Plan. Most of the listed Plans require a minimum of annual training in order to keep employees educated on emergency response procedures in place at the facility. All new employees are required to undergo training on emergency response procedures prior to initiating responsibilities onsite. These Plans also detail best management practices in place at the facility, i.e. good housekeeping, prompt routine equipment maintenance, and inspections.

DESCRIPTION OF STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES:
The CIE ethanol plant is located in Marion, Grant County, Indiana. The facility operates 24 hours per day, 7 days per week for the purpose of manufacturing fuel- and industrial-grade ethanol from grain. The regulated substances stored at the facility are anhydrous ammonia and a flammable mixture - natural gasoline (denaturant). Note that the large final denatured fuel ethanol tank located at this facility is not subject to RMP because the entire mixture does not meet the NFPA-4 criteria.

WORST CASE AND ALTERNATIVE CASE SCENARIOS:
Worst Case Scenarios:
1. Anhydrous Ammonia: Anhydrous Ammonia is stored as a gas liquefied by pressure in an aboveground steel tank. A current SDS for the anhydrous ammonia was us

ed to determine RMP applicability. The worst-case scenario used is a release of the entire contents of the storage vessel, creating a vapor cloud. RMP*Comp was used to determine the worst-case distance to endpoint, 5.4 miles. The ammonia tank sits on a concrete pad, passive mitigation was not included as part of this scenario. Population data was obtained using Circular Area Profiling Software (CAPS) which incorporates 2020 U.S. Census Data. Public receptor information (i.e. schools, hospitals, etc.) was obtained using Google Maps. The towns of Marion and Sweetser, Pipe Creek, Boots Creek, Cart Creek, Sims Franklin Ditch, Sweetsers Ditch, Woods Ditch, Stoney Creek, Lomax Ditch, Lloyd Ditch are within the worst-case distance to the endpoint for ammonia. Environmental receptor information was obtained using a combination of USGS Topographic Map of Grant County and Google Maps. 

2. Flammable Mixture (Denaturant): The flammable mixture stored onsite is natural gasoline, typically referred to as denaturant. Natural gasoline is used onsite to denature ethanol prior to shipment offsite. Denaturant is stored in an aboveground steel tank. The tank is located within a diked containment structure that contains an impermeable liner with gravel overlay. A current SDS for the denaturant was used to determine RMP applicability. The worst-case scenario used is the release of the entire contents of the denaturant tank, causing a vapor cloud explosion. RMP*Comp was used to determine the worst-case distance to endpoint; the model result was a 0.7-mile radius. Population data was obtained using Circular Area Profiling Software (CAPS) which incorporates 2020 U.S. Census Data. Public receptor information (i.e. schools, hospitals, etc.) was obtained using Google Maps. Environmental receptor information was obtained using a combination of USGS Topographic Map of Grant County and Google Maps. No environmental receptors are affected by a worst-case release of denaturant.

Alternative Scenar

ios:
1. Anhydrous Ammonia: The alternate scenario used for anhydrous ammonia is a release due to a ruptured disk/relief valve failure from the ammonia piping system. This scenario is considered the most likely cause of an ammonia release onsite. The alternate release duration assumed is to be 10 minutes with atmospheric stability of D and wind speed of 3.0 m/sec. The facility control room is manned 24 hours/day, 365 days/year and would be alerted of the relief valve failure at the ammonia tank within minutes. The emergency stop would be activated within minutes to shut the entire system down. The emergency shutdown system installed at the facility and the excess flow valve has been considered in this scenario as active mitigation. RMP*Comp was used to determine alternative scenario distance to endpoint; 0.6 miles. Population data was obtained using Circular Area Profiling Software (CAPS) which incorporates 2020 U.S. Census Data. Public receptor information (i.e. schools, hospitals, etc.) was obtained using Google Maps. Environmental receptor information was obtained using a combination of USGS Topographic Map of Grant County and Google Maps. No environmental receptors are affected by an alternative release of anhydrous ammonia.

2. Flammable Mixture (Denaturant): The alternate scenario used for the flammable mixture is the release due to a tanker truck loadout spill, causing a vapor cloud fire. The endpoint used was an over-pressurization of 1 PSI, a worst-case option. Denaturant deliveries at the facility typically occur during normal business hours with a facility staff member overseeing loadout operations - therefore a release at the loadout area could be ceased within minutes by manual overrides. The loadout area also has a catchment basin with underground piping to secondary containment of the tank farm. For this scenario, passive and active mitigation was not considered, as the mitigation strategies currently in place would not contain a vapor cloud fire. RMP*

Comp was used to determine the alternate distance to the endpoint, the model result was a <0.1-mile radius. Population data was obtained using Circular Area Profiling Software (CAPS) which incorporates 2020 U.S. Census Data and showed there are zero residents within the radius. Public receptor information (i.e. schools, hospitals) was obtained using Google Maps. Environmental receptor information was obtained using a combination of USGS Topographic Map of Grant County and Google Maps. No environmental receptors are affected by an alternate release of denaturant. 

Since the facility qualifies as a Program 3 due to the close proximity of public receptors, Process Safety Management has been completed for this facility.

GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS:
Please review the first section of this Executive Summary for the general accidental release prevention program information.

CIE's maintenance department performs regular preventative maintenance inspections, as required by the manufacturer's recommendations and/or State and Federal regulations. Monthly visual inspections are performed, and quarterly leak detection monitoring is performed and reported per IDEM requirements.

FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY:
There have been no reportable accidents associated with RMP-covered processes at the CIE facility.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM:
CIE has developed and implemented an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) that deals with emergency response. The EAP includes information regarding evacuation and response procedures for fires, explosions, spills, etc. CIE is considered a non-responding facility under 40 CFR 68 Subpart E since the facility would evacuate employees and implement the Emergency Action Plan. The facility would also coordinate its emergency response activities with the local Fire Department and Grant County EMA in the event of an emergency involving an anhydrous ammonia or denaturant release. The Plans listed as part of th

is Executive Summary have been prepared in accordance with the applicable regulations, as necessary.

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY:
CIE provides safety training to its employees and contractors on an annual basis. Any changes to improve safety will be implemented immediately upon the discovery of needed changes.

ON-SITE OCA DOCUMENTATION:
CIE maintains records of OCA Documentation on-site. Records include evaluations of worst-case and alternative scenarios identified in this RMP, estimates of quantities released, rate of release, duration of release, methodology used to determine distance to endpoint, and documentation of data used to estimate population & environmental receptors potentially affected by a release of the RMP chemicals.
